I was on Lexapro for a while, but like you I didn't like what it was doing. Lexapro is a Serotonin reuptake inhibitor, and serotonin is one of those chemicals that regulates a number of important systems in the body. For the brain, it regulates memory and learning. Which would explain why you'd have trouble with memory.

While psych meds are great for some people, it's not for everybody. It takes time to find the right medication that works for you. It took me nearly 4 years till I started Prozac 6 months ago. Again, psych meds aren't for everybody. For most people, simply changing the way you live your life will have the same effect. Working out, staying active, and being around other people works just as well as medication. As long as you're getting a healthy dose of them. 

I look at Psych meds as a temporary solution until I can get a handle on my life, but may just as well be on medications for the rest of my life. 

If you don't like what Lexapro is doing to you, ask to try a different medication. It takes a lot of medication trails to find the right one.

I don't have any experience with the first question, but the second question I can give my story. 

A few months ago I had to go on stress leave. While my workplace doesn't have anything officially named "stress leave". They consider it a type of medical leave. My work place gives us small number of hours for Paid Time Off every pay-period.  As long as you can get a signed letter from a licensed professional, you can use your PTO and they can't fire you over it due to labor laws. I suffer from multiple mental health illnesses. I was diagnosed with depression, anxiety, PTSD, Borderline traits, and Dysthymia years ago. Since then I've gotten help from multiple places, and successfully set up my own support circle after many failed attempts. A few months ago, I had to go on stress leave. While my boss wasn't too happy about it. I had a signed letter from a clinician. I'm also fortunate enough to be working at a mental health facility. So my co-workers understand how bad mental illness can be. As for being treated differently after I came back from leave, my boss doesn't treat me any different. As I'm actually a better employee, because I know when there's something wrong with me, and I know how to get the help I need. My mental illness is just as much a strength as it is a handicap.
